To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. CD19 CAR T cell therapy with a 1: 1 CD4+/ CD8+ ratio is feasible in patients with relapsed and refractory B cell malignancies; 2. CD19 CAR expansion and persistence, clinical efficacy, and toxicity are influenced by the lymphodepletion regimen; and 3.
CD19 chimerical antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells with a defined ratio (1:1) of CD4+ to CD8+ T cells have potent antitumor effects in patients with non Hodgkin's Lymphoma.

CD19 specific chimersic antigen receptor ( CAR) modified T cells, when administered in defined CD4+/ CD8+ ratios, can be safely administered to patients with relapsed and refractory non Hodgkin's Lymphoma (NHL).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a CAR T cell manufacturing process with defined CD4+/ CD8+ ratios.
the development of a novel class of immunotherapies for the treatment of B cell malignancies.
the development of novel therapies for patients suffering from cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have demonstrated that the ratio of CD8+/CD4+ CAR T cells has an impact on the efficacy of the treatment.
the authors were able (and did) to identify a subset of CAR T cells that was most likely to result in the best clinical outcomes.
the authors have shown that CD19 specific CAR T cells have potent antitumor efficacy, but that the toxicity profile is variable, with some patients experiencing severe toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD19 CAR T cell therapy is effective and safe in patients with relapsed or refractory non Hodgkin's Lymphoma.
we have developed a manufacturing process to make CAR T cells that have the same phenotype and function every time.

we have developed an approach to manufacture CD19 specific CAR modified T cells from defined T cell populations, which allowed identification of factors that correlate with CAR T cell expansion in vivo, and factors that correlate with the development of severe cytokine release syndrome and neurological toxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD4+/CD 8+ ratio is a critical parameter in the design of CAR T cells and that the ratio of CD8 and CD4 CAR T cells can be manipulated to optimize CAR T cell function.
the CD4+/CD 8+ ratio is important in CAR T cell therapy and that the CD4+ T cell subset is important in CAR expansion and persistence.
the composition of the T cell product is important for efficacy and toxicity.
